foundation.title: Python
foundation.body: Every path starts here. Syntax, data, and how to think in code — then you specialize.

tracks.title: Data Analyst
tracks.tagline: Turn messy tables into decisions leaders can trust.
tracks.for: Beginners, business grads, and anyone who wants a first role in data.

steps.title: Python + spreadsheets
steps.body: Pandas, Excel, and clean data habits. You should be able to load a CSV and answer a business question.

steps.title: SQL
steps.body: Joins, aggregations, window functions. Most analyst interviews live here.

steps.title: BI dashboards
steps.body: Power BI or similar: KPIs, filters, and a story a manager can scan in 30 seconds.

steps.title: Stats for business
steps.body: Averages, trends, A/B intuition — enough to not get fooled by a chart.

steps.title: AI-assisted analysis
steps.body: Use AI to speed cleaning and commentary, then ship a portfolio dashboard.

tracks.title: ML Engineer
tracks.tagline: Take models out of notebooks and into production.
tracks.for: Python developers and data scientists who want systems, not just accuracy.

steps.title: Python engineering
steps.body: Packages, tests, typing. Treat model code like product code.

steps.title: Classical ML depth
steps.body: Feature pipelines, training loops, evaluation you can defend in review.

steps.title: Serving
steps.body: APIs, batch jobs, latency vs throughput. A model that nobody can call is a hobby.

steps.title: MLOps layer
steps.body: Version data and models, CI for training, monitoring drift.

steps.title: Ship a system
steps.body: One project from dataset to trained artifact to endpoint with logs.

tracks.title: LLM Engineer
tracks.tagline: Embeddings, RAG, evals, and inference that actually scales.
tracks.for: Developers who want to specialize in large language models.

steps.title: Python + APIs
steps.body: Call models cleanly. Handle tokens, retries, and cost.

steps.title: Embeddings & retrieval
steps.body: Chunking, vector search, why RAG fails in production.

steps.title: Fine-tuning & PEFT
steps.body: When to fine-tune vs prompt vs retrieve. Measure, don’t guess.

steps.title: Evals
steps.body: Golden sets, hallucination checks, latency/cost tradeoffs.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Batching, caching, safety filters. Optional: LLMOps course next.

tracks.title: MLOps Engineer
tracks.tagline: Pipelines, containers, and reliability for ML and AI services.
tracks.for: Backend or infra people who want to own AI in production.

steps.title: Python + Linux basics
steps.body: Scripts, env management, enough Python to debug a training job.

steps.title: Containers
steps.body: Docker images that train and serve. Repeatable on another machine.

steps.title: CI/CD for models
steps.body: Tests on data contracts, gated deploys, rollback when a model is worse.

steps.title: Orchestration
steps.body: Kubernetes or equivalent: health checks, scaling, secrets.

steps.title: Observe & govern
steps.body: Metrics, cost, drift. Then LLMOps if you are running GenAI.

tracks.title: Data Scientist
tracks.tagline: Python, models, and experiments — not just dashboards.
tracks.for: Analysts who want modeling, or engineers moving into applied ML.

steps.title: Python for science
steps.body: NumPy, Pandas, visualization. Reproducible notebooks, not one-off scripts.

steps.title: Statistics & EDA
steps.body: Distributions, leakage, bias. Learn to distrust a pretty plot.

steps.title: Core machine learning
steps.body: Regression, classification, clustering, evaluation metrics that match the job.

steps.title: Deep learning basics
steps.body: Enough neural nets to use modern tools without cargo-culting.

steps.title: LLMs in the stack
steps.body: RAG and model APIs as products, plus a portfolio that shows end-to-end thinking.

tracks.title: Agentic AI
tracks.tagline: Agents that plan, use tools, and finish multi-step work.
tracks.for: Builders who already know Python and want autonomous workflows.

steps.title: Python + LLM apps
steps.body: Solid API usage and structured outputs before you add loops.

steps.title: Tool use
steps.body: Functions, APIs, files. An agent without tools is a chatbot with extra steps.

steps.title: Planning & memory
steps.body: State, retries, human-in-the-loop. Stop infinite loops.

steps.title: Multi-agent patterns
steps.body: LangGraph-style graphs, roles, handoffs — keep it small and testable.

steps.title: Evaluate agents
steps.body: Task success rate, cost per run, traces. Then ship one real workflow.

tracks.title: AI Developer
tracks.tagline: Ship AI into products: RAG chat, copilots, internal tools.
tracks.for: Software engineers adding GenAI to apps they already build.

steps.title: Python in your stack
steps.body: Or call models from the language you ship — the path still starts with clear APIs.

steps.title: Prompt + product UX
steps.body: Streaming, citations, empty states. Users don’t care about your prompt file.

steps.title: RAG in the app
steps.body: Index company docs, permissions, freshness. Ground answers.

steps.title: Agents when needed
steps.body: Workflows, not demos. Guardrails and logging.

steps.title: Production
steps.body: Auth, rate limits, evals in CI. Optional: full Gen AI specialization.
